# Dick Moore

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025), [v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c31 P28](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0028), [v4 c32 P3](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0003), [v4 c32 P6](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0006)</sub>
- **Role:** Sailor and store clerk  <sub>[v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025), [v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028)</sub>

## Appearance

Dick was a big, handsome man with dashing ways, a higher color than his cousin George, and hair a shade lighter. Like his cousin, he had a unique freak of eyes, with one blue eye and one hazel eye, which was a known Moore family trait.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025), [v4 c11 P27](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0027), [v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015)_

## Personality

Dick had a selfish, disagreeable, and ugly disposition. He was persistent in pursuing what he wanted until he obtained it, after which he lost interest. He was prone to heavy drinking and possessed an unpleasant temper when things did not go his way.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025), [v4 c11 P26](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0026), [v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028)_

## Goals

## History

Dick Moore worked at his father Abner's store at the Glen in the winters and sailed during the summers. He became infatuated with Leslie West due to her beauty, but she repeatedly spurned his advances. To force her into marriage, Dick threatened to have his father foreclose the overdue mortgage on the West farm, prompting Leslie's mother to pressure Leslie into marrying him. Following their quiet wedding, Dick and Leslie lived on the West farm for the winter. In the spring, after Leslie's mother passed away, Dick grew tired of quiet married life and left for Nova Scotia. There, he joined his cousin, George Moore, on a trading voyage aboard the Four Sisters bound for Havana, Cuba. Upon reaching Cuba, Dick contracted yellow fever and died shortly after the ship was forced to sail without him, while George stayed behind to nurse him. For thirteen years, the people of Four Winds mistakenly believed that George Moore—who was brought back suffering from severe amnesia and brain damage—was Dick Moore.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025), [v4 c11 P26](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0026), [v4 c11 P27](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0027), [v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028), [v4 c31 P28](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0028), [v4 c32 P3](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0003), [v4 c32 P6](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0006), [v4 c32 P12](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0012)_
